mainTopic: When limbs count as consumed, לינה on top of the מזבח, and whether כלי שרת make פסולין holy
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a מחלוקת between רבה and רב חסדא about limbs of a קרבן that were off the מזבח at חצות. The question is which later moment makes them count as consumed (עיכול). רב יוסף challenges both of them: maybe חצות makes the limbs consumed wherever they are. Word comes from ארץ ישראל that the הלכה follows him, and two more sources support this. So אביי explains that רבה and רב חסדא only argue about fatty limbs. Next, רבא asks רבה whether לינה disqualifies limbs that spend the night on top of the מזבח and later come down. רבה says there is no לינה there, and the גמרא proves that רבא did not accept this. Finally the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that the מזבח, the כבש and כלי שרת make things holy, bringing a פסוק for each. ריש לקיש then asks רבי יוחנן whether פסולין placed in כלי שרת may be offered on the מזבח לכתחילה. רבי יוחנן says a משנה answers this, and that משנה is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: Second midnight or dawn makes the limbs consumed
steps.stepSummary: רבה ends his ruling: the second חצות makes the limbs consumed. רב חסדא disagrees and says עמוד השחר makes them consumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבה says:] The second midnight makes them consumed. רב חסדא says: Dawn makes them consumed.
steps.whatsHappening: We pick up in the middle of a מחלוקת about limbs that fell off the מזבח before חצות and were put back after חצות. רבה says the next night's חצות makes them consumed, while רב חסדא says the coming עמוד השחר already does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the first חצות makes limbs on the מזבח count as consumed. These limbs missed that moment because they were off the מזבח. The question is which later moment does the job instead: רבה waits for the next חצות, and רב חסדא says עמוד השחר is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Midnight
Makes them consumed (they now count as burned up)
Consumption: the status of limbs that count as burned up, so they need not be put back if they fall
Dawn, the first light of morning

steps.confusionAlert: "Consumed" here does not mean the fire actually finished them. It is a legal status: after this moment, if the limbs fall off the מזבח, you do not have to put them back.

phrases.english: The second midnight makes them consumed,
phrases.notes: This finishes רבה's ruling from the previous page, about limbs that fell off before midnight and were put back after midnight.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says:
Dawn makes them consumed.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲצוֹת שֵׁנִי עוֹכַלְתָּן, רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מחלוקת from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: the second חצות makes the limbs consumed. רב חסדא: עמוד השחר makes them consumed.

steps.title: Asking for רב חסדא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The students of בי רב ask what reasoning lies behind רב חסדא's view that dawn makes the limbs consumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the school of רב: What is the reason of רב חסדא?
steps.whatsHappening: The students of בי רב ask why רב חסדא thinks dawn makes the limbs consumed. This question sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody has explained yet why עמוד השחר should take the place of חצות. The גמרא wants the logic behind רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They say in the school of רב
What is the reason?

phrases.english: They say in the school of Rav:
What is the reason of Rav Ḥisda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב חסדא's ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would עמוד השחר make the limbs consumed?

steps.title: A קל וחומר from midnight to dawn
steps.stepSummary: Answer: חצות does not cause לינה, yet it causes עיכול. עמוד השחר does cause לינה, so surely it also causes עיכול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If midnight, which does not cause the problem of being left overnight, still causes consumption, then dawn, which does cause the problem of being left overnight, surely causes consumption!
steps.whatsHappening: The students answer with a קל וחומר: dawn is a "stronger" moment than midnight, so if midnight can make limbs consumed, dawn certainly can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לינה means limbs that stay off the מזבח until a certain time become פסול. That happens at עמוד השחר, not at חצות. Since dawn has more legal power in the area of לינה, it should also have the power of עיכול that the weaker moment, חצות, already has.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if…" (opens a קל וחומר)
Being left overnight, which disqualifies limbs not on the מזבח by dawn
Isn't it logical? (the closing of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's view rests on a קל וחומר: עמוד השחר, which causes לינה, is stronger than חצות, so it can also cause עיכול.

phrases.english: And if midnight, which does not cause "left overnight,"
still causes consumption;
dawn, which does cause "left overnight,"
isn't it logical that it causes consumption?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: since עמוד השחר causes לינה and חצות does not, dawn should surely cause עיכול just as midnight does.

steps.title: Second case: limbs that missed both midnight and dawn
steps.stepSummary: Limbs fell off before חצות and were put back only after עמוד השחר. רבה: the second חצות makes them consumed. רב חסדא: they never become consumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they separated before midnight and he returned them after dawn, רבה says: the second midnight makes them consumed. רב חסדא says: they never become consumed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second argument between the same two אמוראים, this time about limbs that were off the מזבח at both חצות and עמוד השחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה stays consistent: the next חצות does the job. רב חסדא says that once these limbs missed dawn too, no later moment makes them consumed, so they must keep burning until they are fully burned up. Both cases show that רבה and רב חסדא agree on one thing: חצות works only on limbs that are on top of the מזבח at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: They separated (fell off the מזבח)
And he put them back
Ever, never

phrases.english: If they separated before midnight,
and he put them back after dawn –
Rabba says: The second midnight makes them consumed,
Rav Ḥisda says:
They never become consumed.
phrases.notes: He means time alone never makes them count as burned; they just stay on the fire until they turn to ash.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירְשׁוּ קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת, וְהֶחְזִירָן לְאַחַר עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case: the limbs now miss dawn as well as midnight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: the second חצות makes them consumed. רב חסדא: they never become consumed through time.

steps.title: רב יוסף: maybe midnight works wherever the limbs are
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges what both sides assumed: who says חצות only makes limbs consumed when they are on the מזבח? Maybe it works wherever they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: Who tells us that midnight makes them consumed only on top of the altar? Maybe wherever they are found, it makes them consumed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the shared assumption behind both arguments. Maybe the first חצות makes the limbs consumed even if they had fallen off the מזבח at that moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבה and רב חסדא were looking for a later moment to replace the first חצות, because they assumed חצות only works on the מזבח. If רב יוסף is right, the first חצות already made these limbs consumed, and the whole search for a replacement is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it
And who will tell us?
Perhaps
On top of the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
And who will tell us
that midnight, on top of the altar,
is what makes them consumed?
Perhaps wherever it finds them,
it makes them consumed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption shared by both sides in steps 1 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shared assumption of רבה and רב חסדא that חצות makes limbs consumed only when they are on the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no proof for that limit. חצות might make the limbs consumed wherever they are, so the first חצות would already work and no replacement moment is needed.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: Word is sent from ארץ ישראל that the הלכה follows רב יוסף: חצות makes the limbs consumed wherever they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: The הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל send a ruling that the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the first חצות makes the limbs consumed even if they were off the מזבח at that time. For ordinary limbs, this makes both רבה's and רב חסדא's searches for a later moment unnecessary. Steps 8-9 show where their debate still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)
The practical הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: once חצות passes, the limbs count as consumed wherever they are, on the מזבח or not. That follows רב יוסף.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling rejects the assumption that רבה and רב חסדא shared. This forces the גמרא, in Steps 8-9, to find a narrower case (fatty limbs) where their debate still applies.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
The halacha follows Rav Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the הלכה in favor of רב יוסף's objection in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חצות makes the limbs consumed wherever they are.

steps.title: Support for רב יוסף from רבי חייא בר אבא and בר קפרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא and a ברייתא of בר קפרא both rule that limbs which were off the מזבח at חצות are no longer subject to מעילה. This shows that חצות made them consumed even though they were not on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי חייא בר אבא said that if limbs fell off before midnight and were put back after midnight, one may not use them, but there is no מעילה. בר קפרא also taught that in such a case they leave the status of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two more sources that agree with רב יוסף's ruling from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limbs were off the מזבח at midnight, yet the מעילה status ends. מעילה ends only once a limb is treated as consumed. So these sources show that חצות makes limbs consumed wherever they are, just as רב יוסף said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: brings another source saying the same thing
They came off (the limbs separated from the מזבח)
One may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for מעילה
Misusing הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
If the limbs came off before midnight
and he put them back after midnight,
one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.
phrases.notes: There is no מעילה because the limbs already count as consumed, even though they were off the מזבח at midnight.

phrases.english: And בר קפרא taught the same:
If they came off before midnight
and he put them back after midnight,
they leave the status of מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds supporting sources for the הלכה like רב יוסף from Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that חצות makes limbs consumed even off the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רבי חייא בר אבא and a ברייתא taught by בר קפרא.

steps.title: Then what do רבה and רב חסדא argue about?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if the הלכה is that חצות works anywhere, the case where limbs fell off before midnight should be simple. So what is the argument between רבה and רב חסדא about?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Since they sent from there that the הלכה follows רב יוסף, and רבי חייא בר אבא said so, and בר קפרא taught so, what do רבה and רב חסדא argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges both arguments between רבה and רב חסדא, in Steps 1 and 4. Once the הלכה follows רב יוסף, those arguments seem to have no subject left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב חסדא argued about limbs that were off the מזבח at midnight. If midnight makes them consumed anyway, both should agree they are consumed. So the argument seems to have no case left.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, meaning from ארץ ישראל
The הלכה, the final ruling
About what do they argue?

phrases.english: רב פפא said to אביי:
Since they sent from there
that the הלכה follows רב יוסף,
and רבי חייא בר אבא said so,
and בר קפרא taught so as well,
then about what do רבה and רב חסדא argue?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דִּשְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם הִילְכְתָא כְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the accepted הלכה from Steps 6-7 to question both arguments in Steps 1 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both arguments between רבה and רב חסדא, in Steps 1 and 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חצות makes limbs consumed anywhere, then limbs off the מזבח at midnight are clearly consumed. The argument then seems to have no subject.

steps.title: They argue about fatty limbs
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבה and רב חסדא argue about fatty limbs. For those, midnight may not make them consumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: They argue about fatty limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא by limiting the argument to one special kind of limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that חצות makes limbs consumed anywhere still stands for normal limbs. Fatty limbs are different, so for them the question of what happens off the מזבח is still open. That is where רבה and רב חסדא disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Fatty limbs

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רב יוסף: חצות makes ordinary limbs consumed wherever they are. The argument of רבה and רב חסדא is kept only for fatty limbs.

phrases.english: He said to him: about fatty limbs.
phrases.notes: אביי is saying their whole argument is only about fatty limbs, not ordinary ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the argument of רבה and רב חסדא had no case left once the הלכה followed רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about fatty limbs, where midnight may not make them consumed.

steps.title: Does being left overnight disqualify limbs on top of the altar?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה a new question: does לינה disqualify limbs that spend the night on top of the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רבה: Does being left overnight disqualify limbs on top of the מזבח, or does it not disqualify them there?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבא asks whether staying overnight on top of the מזבח makes limbs פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know that being left overnight can make sacrifices פסול. The question is whether the top of the מזבח itself protects them from this, or whether the disqualification works even there.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question)
Being left overnight takes effect (disqualifies)
The top of the מזבח

phrases.english: רבא asked רבה:
Does being left overnight disqualify on top of the מזבח,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינָהּ מוֹעֶלֶת בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ?
phrases.english: or does it not disqualify on top of the מזבח?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the midnight discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether לינה disqualifies limbs that spent the night on top of the מזבח.

steps.title: If they never came down, the answer is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבא means. If the limbs stayed on the מזבח, the answer is obvious. The משנה already said that limbs left overnight in the עזרה may stay once they go up, so limbs on top of the מזבח surely may stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say they did not come down, then now that for limbs left overnight in the courtyard you said they should not come down, is it even a question for limbs on top of the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible meaning of רבא's question and shows it cannot be what he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. Limbs that spent the night down in the עזרה are not taken down once they go up on the מזבח. Limbs that spent the night on top of the מזבח are in a better position, so they surely stay.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case?
If you say (suggests a meaning, often to reject it)
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that they did not come down,
now, about limbs left overnight in the courtyard,
you said that they should not come down,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה earlier in the פרק: once such limbs went up on the מזבח, they are not taken down.

phrases.english: so for limbs on top of the מזבח, is it even a question?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case רבא's question in Step 10 is about.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבא's question as being about limbs that never came down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the משנה: if limbs left overnight in the עזרה stay up once raised, limbs left on the מזבח surely stay. So there would be nothing to ask.

steps.title: Is the altar top like the Table or like the floor?
steps.stepSummary: So the question must be about limbs that came down after dawn. Do we treat the top of the מזבח like the שלחן, where staying many days does no harm, or like the floor, where staying overnight makes them פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where they came down. Do we compare it to the שלחן? As we learned: even if the loaves stay on the שלחן many days, there is nothing wrong. Or perhaps we compare it to the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case of רבא's question. It then lays out the two ways one could compare it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limbs stayed on top of the מזבח past dawn and then came down. If the מזבח top is like the שלחן, a holy place where overnight does no harm, they are still fine and go back up. If it is like the floor of the עזרה, the night made them פסול and they do not go back up.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare it to
The Table of the לחם הפנים in the היכל
The ground (floor of the עזרה)
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about limbs that stayed on the מזבח the whole time. That case was already called obvious in Step 11. It is about limbs that spent the night on top and came down after dawn.

phrases.english: Rather, the case is where they came down;
do we compare it to the Table?
As we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֵן עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים –
phrases.english: Even if they stay on the Table many days,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the loaves of לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: there is nothing wrong with that.
Or perhaps we compare it to the ground?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from Step 11 with the real case, and frames the doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the top of the מזבח protects against לינה like the שלחן, or does not protect, like the floor of the עזרה.

steps.title: רבה answers: no overnight problem on top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers רבא that there is no לינה on top of the מזבח, so limbs that came down after dawn may go back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: There is no disqualification of לינה on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רבא's question from Step 12. The top of the מזבח is like the שלחן, so spending the night there does not make limbs פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked whether the top of the מזבח is like the שלחן or like the floor. רבה picks the שלחן side. Limbs that spent the night up there and then fell down after dawn are still fine, and they can go back up.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying overnight; something left past dawn becomes פסול
The top of the מזבח

phrases.english: He said to him:
There is no disqualification of overnight on top of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין לִינָה בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The top of the מזבח is like the שלחן: לינה there does not make limbs פסול.

steps.title: Did רבא accept רבה's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא agreed with רבה's answer or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he accept it from him, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבא was convinced by his teacher רבה's answer. It is setting up a proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student sometimes hears his teacher's answer and still disagrees. The גמרא wants to know whether רבא kept his own view. The answer will come from a later statement where רבה and רבא argue.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it from him

phrases.english: Did he accept it from him, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבא reacted to רבה's answer in Step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא accepted רבה's ruling that there is no לינה on top of the מזבח

steps.title: Proof from a later argument between רבה and רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching about limbs left overnight, and then a מחלוקת: for limbs that came down, רבה says they go back up and רבא says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what was stated: Limbs that stayed overnight in the עזרה may keep being burned all night. A limb that stayed overnight on top of the מזבח may be burned forever. If they came down: רבה says they go back up, and רבא says they do not go back up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching to answer its question. In a case of limbs that came down from the top of the מזבח, רבה and רבא give opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the teaching gives two rules. Limbs left in the עזרה may still be put up during that night. Limbs left on top of the מזבח may be burned at any time later. Then comes the real question, limbs that came down. Here רבה says יעלו, which matches his answer in Step 13, while רבא says לא יעלו.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep on burning
They go back up / they do not go back up
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Come and hear, for it was stated:
Limbs that stayed overnight in the courtyard –
he may keep on burning them all night.
If it stayed overnight on top of the altar –
he may keep on burning it forever.
If they came down –
Rabba says: They should go back up,
Rava says: They should not go back up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence to answer the question in Step 14
steps.raayaSupportSource: An אמורא teaching where רבה and רבא argue about limbs that came down from the top of the מזבח

steps.title: Conclusion: רבא did not accept it
steps.stepSummary: Since רבא rules that the limbs do not go back up, he must not have accepted רבה's answer. The גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: he did not accept it from him! Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the מחלוקת. רבא kept his own view, and the גמרא confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא had accepted that there is no לינה on top of the מזבח, he would say the limbs may go back up. Since he says לא יעלו, he must hold that the top of the מזבח is like the floor. The closing שמע מינה means the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; when repeated, it confirms the proof

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: no לינה on top of the מזבח, so limbs that came down go back up. רבא disagrees and says they do not go back up.

phrases.english: Learn from this: he did not accept it from him!
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from the proof in Step 15
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא did not accept רבה's answer. He holds that לינה does make limbs פסול even on top of the מזבח.

steps.title: Sources that the altar, ramp and vessels make things holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the מזבח making things holy. A ברייתא finds a פסוק for the מזבח, the כבש and כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says, "Just as the מזבח makes things holy..." The Rabbis taught: "Whatever touches the מזבח" teaches only about the מזבח. Where do we learn the כבש? The פסוק says "את המזבח." Where do we learn כלי שרת? The פסוק says, "Whatever touches them shall become holy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. Then it brings a ברייתא that gives a source for each item the משנה lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק only mentions the מזבח. The extra word את adds the כבש, the ramp leading up to the מזבח. A different פסוק about the vessels of the משכן gives the same power to כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes holy; once something is on it, it must stay there
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Holy vessels used in the עבודה
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: Just as the altar sanctifies, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה; the "etc." stands for the rest: so too the ramp and the vessels.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Whatever touches the altar" –
I only know about the altar;
From where do we know the ramp?
The verse says: "the altar [et hamizbe'ach]."
phrases.notes: שמות 40:10. The extra word את comes to include the כבש.

phrases.english: From where do we know service vessels?
The verse says: "Whatever touches them shall become holy."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְקַדֵּשׁ כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח, the כבש and כלי שרת all make things holy, each learned from a פסוק.

steps.title: Do service vessels make disqualified items holy?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether כלי שרת make even פסולין holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: Do כלי שרת make פסולין holy?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks a new question about כלי שרת. He wants to know whether their power reaches even items that are already פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the מזבח keeps certain פסולין that went up on it. The question is whether a vessel has the same strength, or whether it only makes kosher items holy.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question of learning)
Items that are unfit for the עבודה
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked Rabbi Yochanan:
Service vessels, what is the law,
do they make the disqualified items holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 17's source that כלי שרת make things holy
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כלי שרת make פסולין holy the way the מזבח does

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: you already learned it in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers from the משנה: just as the מזבח and the כבש make holy what is suited to them, so do the vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it already. Just as the מזבח and the כבש make holy what is suited to them, so the vessels make things holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers yes, and shows that the answer is already in the משנה. The משנה compares the vessels to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח and the כבש make holy even פסולין, as long as the item is the kind that belongs on them. Because the משנה says the vessels work כשם, "just like" the מזבח, they also make פסולין holy.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a משנה)
What is suited to them
So too

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: כלי שרת make פסולין holy just like the מזבח, because the משנה compares them.

phrases.english: He said to him, you learned it:
Just as the altar and the ramp
sanctify what is suited to them,
so too the vessels sanctify!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question in Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The משנה compares the vessels to the מזבח and the כבש, which make holy even פסולין that are suited to them.

steps.title: ריש לקיש clarifies: he is asking about offering them from the start
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה's rule does not answer him. He wants to know whether פסולין placed in כלי שרת may be offered on the מזבח לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: I am asking whether they may be offered from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer. He says the משנה does not touch his real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that כלי שרת make things holy. That means a פסול item placed in them can no longer be redeemed and taken out to חולין. ריש לקיש is asking about something further: may that item actually be brought up on the מזבח לכתחילה? Being 'made holy' and being 'allowed to be offered' are two different levels.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; as the proper way to act, not only after the fact
To be offered on the מזבח
I am asking about; this is my question

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying the vessels fail to make פסולין holy. He accepts that they do. He is only asking whether that holiness goes far enough to let the item be offered from the start.

phrases.english: He said to him: whether they may be offered from the start
phrases.notes: Here ריש לקיש is speaking to רבי יוחנן. The משנה only showed that the items can no longer be redeemed.

phrases.english: is what I am asking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְכַתְּחִילָּה לִיקְרַב קָמִיבְּעֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside step 19's answer by sharpening the question from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה. It does not reject what the משנה itself teaches.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה only teaches that the vessels make the item holy, so it cannot be redeemed. It does not say whether the item may be offered לכתחילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says this too is taught in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that even the sharper question is answered by a משנה. The גמרא will quote that משנה next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן answered: We learned this too in a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי יוחנן starts a new answer and says a משנה covers this too, and the גמרא will quote that משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not argue with ריש לקיש's clarification. Instead he says that even the question of offering לכתחילה is already settled by a משנה. The actual proof only comes in the quote that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: This too

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
phrases.notes: Now רבי יוחנן is answering. The משנה he means is quoted right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharper question from step 20 by announcing a proof from a משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether פסולין made holy by כלי שרת may be offered on the מזבח לכתחילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A משנה already teaches the answer. The quote comes next.
